nodes.title: Statement of Erdős Problem 793

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $F(n)$ is the largest size of a good subset of $\{1, \dots, n\}$, defined as the supremum of the sizes of the good sets $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$.
nodes.title: Maximum size of a good subset

nodes.summary: A finite set $A$ of natural numbers is good when every element of $A$ is positive and no $a \in A$ divides $bc$ for any $b, c \in A$ with $a \ne b$ and $a \ne c$; here $b = c$ is allowed.
